claim: Suleymanova's arXiv:1710.05355 studies how vanishing of the logarithmic heat-trace coefficient (present generically for conic singularities) relates to smoothness of the singular cross-section, in general dimension, and reports this remains an open/unresolved characterization beyond dimension 4 and cyclic space forms.
stance_target: State of the general-dimension conic-singularity heat-trace literature as of 2017
scope_conditions: General-dimension Riemannian manifolds with isolated conic singularities and constant-curvature cross sections
quoted_support: In higher dimensions the situation is naturally more difficult. We illustrate this in the case of cross sections with constant curvature. Then the logarithmic term becomes a polynomial in the curvature with roots that are different from 1, which necessitates more vanishing of other terms, not isolated so far.

claim: arXiv:1710.05355 is unpublished (no journal-ref, only the arXiv DataCite DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1710.05355), and is distinct from both arXiv:1701.01874 (the prequel general-expansion paper) and arXiv:1711.00577 (the 2-dimensional surfaces paper).
stance_target: Publication record and relationship among Suleymanova's 2017 conic-singularity preprints
quoted_support: In the previous article we derived a detailed asymptotic expansion of the heat trace for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions on manifolds with conic singularities. In this article we investigate how the terms in the expansion reflect the geometry of the manifold.
